data.long_meaning: The name Severin is derived from the Latin word 'severus', which means 'severe' or 'stern'. In ancient Rome, the name was given to children as a sign of respect and admiration for their parents' severity and steadfastness. The name was also associated with the god Severus, who was believed to protect against fire and storms. In Christian tradition, Severin is the name of several saints, including St. Severin of Noricum, who was a bishop and martyr, and St. Severin of Cologne, who was a missionary and bishop.

historical_references.reference: Saint Severinus of Noricum was a bishop who lived in the 5th century. He is venerated as a saint in the Roman Catholic Church and the Eastern Orthodox Church. He was born in Noricum, a Roman province in present-day Austria. Severinus was a hermit who lived in a cave in the Alps and was ordained a bishop in 420 AD by Saint Germanus of Auxerre. He became a respected figure in the region and founded several monasteries and churches.

historical_references.reference: Saint Severinus of Cologne, also known as Severinus of Quirites, was a hermit who lived in the 7th century. He is venerated as a saint in the Roman Catholic Church and the Eastern Orthodox Church. He was born in Italy and was originally a soldier in the Roman army. After a vision, he left the army and became a hermit in the forest of the Rhine River in present-day Germany. He founded the towns of Cologne and Xanten, and is the patron saint of Cologne.
